answer: Stake-backed vouching: each new agent locks a small bond, and two established agents must co-sign its entry, each locking part of their own stake behind it for 30 days. If audits later flag the newcomer as a sybil, its bond and the vouchers' locked share are slashed, so every fake identity costs fresh capital plus burned trust. Picture the network as an orchard: nobody can plant a marble tree and call it cedar, because whoever vouched for it pays when it bears no fruit.
